title: Use pandas .array, not .to_numpy, when moving nullable outputs into the eval table
answers: Int64 predictions lose precision in evaluation table
large integers corrupted to float in eval results table with pd.NA
nullable integer outputs become wrong values after evaluate
to_numpy converts pandas nullable dtype and corrupts values
body:
Symptom: Large integer model outputs with missing values (for example Int64 with pd.NA near 2**63-1) come back from the evaluation table with corrupted values.
Root cause: converting a nullable pandas Series with `.to_numpy()` coerces it to a lossy dtype (object or float) when NA is present, so integers past float precision change silently.
Fix pattern: Use `.array` (the ExtensionArray) to hand the values to the table builder; it preserves the nullable dtype and the exact values.
Constraints: Regression coverage is test_evaluation_table_preserves_nullable_integer_outputs in tests/evaluate/test_default_evaluator.py, which checks the value 2**63-1 round-trips with None for the NA. Prefer `.array` over `.to_numpy()` for any output moved into this table.
applies: Applies to evaluation-table construction in the default evaluator for pandas extension dtypes (Int64, boolean, etc.); plain numpy-backed Series are unaffected.
says: Large integer predictions containing missing values are displayed with corrupted numbers after evaluation.
Model evaluation results show incorrect values for large numbers when empty rows exist.
The model evaluation table should preserve exact precision for big numbers with missing entries.
Large numbers in model predictions unexpectedly convert to inaccurate decimal values during evaluation.
search: In mlflow/models/evaluation/default_evaluator.py, evaluation-table construction must pass pandas extension dtypes using .array rather than .to_numpy(). Converting nullable Series with .to_numpy() coerces missing values into lossy float or object types, corrupting large integers like 2**63-1. Applies to default evaluator table construction for pandas extension dtypes like Int64 and boolean, while plain numpy-backed Series remain unaffected. Regression coverage is enforced by test_evaluation_table_preserves_nullable_integer_outputs in tests/evaluate/test_default_evaluator.py.
